findings.question: Q1
findings.finding: Rebuilt from Tilray's own disclosures, Q1 FY27 revenue lands near $270m (range $262-280m), about 1.5% above the $264.9-268.2m consensus: organic revenue grew only +2.7% y/y in Q4 FY26 ($281.7m less $51.1m BrewDog = $230.6m vs $224.5m) and EUR/CAD averaged 1-2% weaker y/y in Jun-Aug, so organic Q1 is ~$213m; BrewDog adds ~$52-62m (Q4 $51.1m for its first ~3 months; 10-K pro forma $190.2m for the 9 pre-acquisition months, before 38 bars were shut; UK pub LFL +4.2% in World Cup July and +2.4% in August), while US craft beer ran -7% $ / -9% volume in late July-August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 revenue $281.7m vs $240.8-246.3m consensus (+14-17%): next session -0.99% (baseline 2026-07-28, 247wallst/goldesel bars). Q3 FY26 'record' revenue: -5.1% (2026-04-01). This name has not paid for revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus ($264.9-268.2m) sits within $2-5m of Q4 revenue times Tilray's own Q1/Q4 seasonal ratio (209.5/224.5 = 0.933 -> $262.9m), i.e. it carries BrewDog with Tilray's spring-loaded US-beer seasonality rather than the UK summer peak; had the summer/World Cup trade been modelled, estimates would sit at $270m+. The gap is small and the reaction function vetoes most of it.
findings.independence: UK on-trade tracker (CGA/NIQ) July and August 2026, a different source: https://nielseniq.com/global/en/news-center/2026/world-cup-scores-for-pubs-in-july-but-restaurant-sales-flag-in-the-heat/ ; the negative US craft read is Circana via vinetur (snippet_only, 429 on fetch): https://www.vinetur.com/en/20260825106088/us-beer-sales-fell-44-in-the-four-weeks-ending-aug-15.html. findings.question: Q2
findings.finding: The $68-75m FY27 adj EBITDA guide carries a cost headwind nothing shows the street has modelled: Q4 FY26 already absorbed $2.3m of 'unanticipated fuel surcharges' (CFO), US diesel averaged $5.16/gal in Jun-Aug 2026 (+40% y/y, only 3% below the Q4 level) and has risen to $6.20-6.29 since the 2026-07-28 guide (+17%; Brent $85.51 -> $125.44), EU gas ran $17.93/MMBtu in July (+56% y/y), and the 10-K added an Iran-conflict risk factor naming fuel and energy for brewing and cultivation; management's documented habit (reconfirmed FY26 at Q3 while flagging fuel, then printed $61.1m under the $62m low end and quoted it 'ex-fuel') makes an outright cut unlikely and a qualified or 'ex-fuel' reaffirmation plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide cuts: 2025-04-08 -20.69%, 2025-01-10 -10.22%. Reaffirm plus net income: 2025-10-09 +22.09%. Reconfirm while flagging fuel risk: 2026-04-01 -5.1%. First FY27 guide (reported as below expectations by a search synthesis, unverified): 2026-07-28 -0.99%.
findings.why_not_priced: Anchoring on the company's guide and stale estimates: the guide is 71 days old and no estimate revision, preview or note found since quantifies fuel (EarningsWhispers 2026-09-30 frames the quarter only as a checkpoint on $68-75m). TLRY's -19% since 2026-08-26 matches the Canadian cannabis group (CGC -15%, OGI -23.5%, SNDL -10%) and the 2026-09-29 DEA pause, so the drawdown is not a guide-specific discount. Priced would look like FY27 EBITDA estimates below $68m or previews flagging fuel; neither found. Size is small because the incremental cost vs what management could see on 07-28 is ~$1.5-3m (diesel +13-19%), not the Brent-from-trough $6-9m.
findings.independence: Company-confirmed transmission in two other documents: CFO quote on fuel surcharges (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/TLRY/Q42026) and the 10-K risk factor (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1731348/000143774926024698/tlry20260531_10k.htm); price series from FRED (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DDFUELNYH, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=PNGASEUUSDM, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=DCOILBRENTEU). findings.question: Q3

Against an easy comp (Q1 FY26 cannabis $64.5m at a 36% gross margin vs 44% in Q4 FY26), Tilray's cannabis revenue should grow mid-to-high single digits with margin up several points, net of CAD -2% y/y, ~$21m/yr international price compression and Tilray growing below the German market (+25% in FY26 while Remexian's share went 6.5% -> 10.5%).

findings.why_not_priced: The read-through is a competitor's and a peer's print dated after Tilray last spoke; ACB (+64%) and HITI (+29%) re-rated on international medical since 2026-07-27 while TLRY fell 7%, so the market has not carried it to TLRY. Sized small because Tilray is losing German share and the line has not moved this stock.

baseline_tension: The findings net slightly negative against a call-bid skew (-12) and a crowded short, and the -11.5% 20-day run-up is sector-driven (DEA pause 09-29; CGC -15%, OGI -23.5% since 08-26) rather than a discount for these negatives, so p_up is held near 50 (48) rather than leaning harder.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): Q1 revenue finding 0.3 -> 0.2 and Q3 cannabis 0.3 -> 0.2; this name sold a 14-17% revenue beat (-0.99%) and a +73% international quarter (-5.1%).

Rule 3 (own caveat reaches the number): Q2 guide finding -1.0 -> -0.5; management's documented habit of reconfirming through the April fuel spike, plus the diesel series I read after the freeze (diesel never troughed with Brent, so the incremental cost vs the 07-28 guide is ~$1.5-3m, not $6-9m), cut the probability of a cut or qualification.

Rule 4 (financing is a question): dilution finding -0.5 -> -0.3; answer obtained: no visible ramp to fund, no distress (net debt $0.7m), notes being retired with stock; a dilution habit, not a solvency signal.

Rule 7 (positioning): crowded short (19.4m, DTC 5.2) and call-bid skew kept as ONE positive positioning finding, trimmed 0.5 -> 0.3 because the July print with similar positioning gave no day-one squeeze; the negatives were not shrunk a second time for the same short.

Rule 6 (verify the bar): revenue bar from two sources within 1.3% ($264.9m, $268.2m); no Q1 EBITDA consensus could be sourced, so nothing is sized on an EBITDA beat or miss; an unverified '$84m FY27 consensus' was rejected as unsourced.
Scaled measurement: p_up held at 48 (5 of 7 prior prints fell; the dilution habit) and nudged no further toward 50; abs_move_pct left at 9.5 per rule 8 (understatement is the systematic error).

Net: pre-lessons sum -0.4 -> -0.1. The trims were larger on the negative side (guide -1.0 -> -0.5 on management's reconfirm habit and the diesel series; dilution -0.5 -> -0.3) than on the positive side (revenue, cannabis and positioning each -0.1 to -0.2); print_vs_bar_pct 2.0 -> 1.5 after the FX-adjusted rebuild.

investment_decision.reason: The two reported-quarter questions came back close to their priced answers: revenue ~1.5% above a $265-268m consensus (Q1) and cannabis modestly better on an easy comp (Q3), on lines this stock has not paid for. The one answer the price does not hold is a fuel and energy headwind against a 71-day-old guide (Q2), but diesel never troughed with Brent and management reaffirms through such headwinds, so it is a tail rather than the base case; it is offset by a crowded short into a sector washout, and the dilution residual (Q5) is small. impact_sum -0.1 and impact_scaled -0.38 against a +/-10.9% implied move are noise; the decision agrees with a near-zero sum.
investment_decision.what_would_change_it: Explicit language cutting or qualifying the $68-75m FY27 guide (low end, 'excluding fuel surcharges') would make it a short; a clean reaffirm with Q1 adj EBITDA of $15m or more would make it a squeeze long.
